key_insight: ConsID-Gen combines data-level multi-view enrichment with model-level identity and view-consistency objectives to generate temporally coherent videos from a single image while preserving fine-grained object identity across viewpoint changes.
problem_solved: Addresses appearance drift and geometric distortion in image-to-video generation where single-view inputs and weak cross-modal alignment cause loss of identity and inconsistent views over time.
method: Augment training data with synthesized or multi-view examples to reduce single-view sparsity and expose varied viewpoints.
Introduce view-consistency and identity-preserving losses that explicitly penalize appearance drift and geometric inconsistency across generated frames.
Improve cross-modal alignment between image, text instruction, and video representations (e.g., via attention/feature matching) so animations follow instructions while retaining object identity.
impact: Enables more reliable, identity-faithful I2V pipelines useful for avatar animation, film VFX, and content creation where preserving object/person likeness across camera motion is critical. Practitioners get a practical recipe (data + loss + alignment) to reduce common I2V artifacts.
visual_elements: Before/After frame sequence: static input image → baseline I2V (shows drift) → ConsID-Gen output (maintained identity) to illustrate improvement.
Pipeline diagram: data augmentation (multi-view) → model with identity & view-consistency losses → generated video, annotated with loss icons.
Frame-level consistency chart: quantitative plot showing reduced identity/appearance error over time compared to baselines.
Attention/feature-map visualization: overlays showing where the model preserves identity features across frames.
paper_title: ConsID-Gen: View-Consistent and Identity-Preserving Image-to-Video Generation
paper_authors: Mingyang Wu, Ashirbad Mishra, Soumik Dey, Shuo Xing, Naveen Ravipati
